mainTopic: The timing of תרומת הדשן, the meaning of קריאת הגבר, and side teachings about great voices and sounds
overview: The גמרא rejects the idea that doing תרומת הדשן from חצות is a Torah law, because the משנה lets us do it earlier on רגלים and later on regular days. רבי יוחנן brings a different source from the פסוק: the extra words 'עד הבקר' mean rising before dawn, with no fixed hour. The גמרא then explains the three times in the משנה (regular days, יום הכפורים, רגלים) as practical choices based on need. Next comes a dispute about קריאת הגבר: רב says it is a man's call, and רבי שילא says it is a rooster's crow. A story follows in which רב serves as רבי שילא's speaker, defends his reading, and refuses to step down out of respect for the role. A ברייתא about גביני the crier supports רב, and this leads to comparisons of how far גביני's voice and the כהן גדול's voice carried. The גמרא ends with side teachings about why voices carry less by day and which great sounds travel across the world. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If midnight were Torah law, how could we move the time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that תרומת הדשן from חצות is a Torah law. The משנה lets us do it earlier on רגלים and later on regular days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that 'from midnight' is a Torah law, how could we do it earlier, and how could we do it later?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion that the time for תרומת הדשן is fixed at חצות by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the כהנים start at the first watch on רגלים, which is before חצות. On regular days they start around the rooster's call, which is after חצות. A Torah-fixed time could not be moved in both directions like that, so the suggestion cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind (to say)
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא tries out an idea, only to show it doesn't work.

phrases.english: that 'from midnight' is Torah law,
how do we do it earlier
phrases.notes: On the רגלים the משנה says they start from the first watch.

phrases.english: (and how do we do it later)?
phrases.notes: On regular days they start around the rooster's call, after midnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מֵחֲצוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier suggestion (on the previous amud) that תרומת הדשן from חצות is a Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the time of תרומת הדשן is fixed at חצות by Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah-fixed time cannot be moved both earlier and later. Yet the משנה moves it both ways, earlier on רגלים and later on regular days.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'until morning' means rise before morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a new reading of the פסוק. The extra words 'עד הבקר' teach us to add a 'morning' before the real morning. This means the תרומת הדשן is done before dawn, with no fixed hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: Since the verse says 'all night,' don't I already know it means until morning? So why does the verse add 'until morning'? It means: give a 'morning' to the morning of the night.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first idea failed, רבי יוחנן gives a different source from the פסוק. It teaches that the work starts before dawn but sets no exact hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כל הלילה' already implies 'until morning,' so the words 'עד הבקר' seem extra. רבי יוחנן reads them as a second, earlier 'morning': get up before the real dawn. Because no exact hour is given, the timing can change depending on need.

keyTerms.meaning: All night (from the פסוק about burning the limbs)
Why does the verse need to say this? (pointing to extra words)
Give a 'morning' to the night's morning, meaning start before dawn

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not setting a new fixed hour to replace חצות. His point is that the Torah only requires starting before dawn, so the exact time is flexible.
steps.whyThisMatters: This flexibility is what explains how the משנה can give three different start times without any of them being a Torah requirement.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: 'אלא' signals that the rejected idea is being replaced.

phrases.english: From the fact that it says: 'all night,'
don't I know that it means until morning?
So why does the verse say 'until morning'?
phrases.notes: The words seem extra, so they must teach something new.

phrases.english: Give a 'morning' to the morning of the night.
phrases.notes: Add an earlier 'morning': start before dawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected idea of a Torah-fixed חצות with a flexible source from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement source: a new reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the time was fixed at חצות by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah only requires starting before dawn, so the exact hour can change depending on need.

steps.title: Applying the rule to regular days, יום הכפורים, and רגלים
steps.stepSummary: Based on רבי יוחנן's flexible rule, the גמרא explains the three times in the משנה. Each time fits the needs of that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: Every day, they remove the ashes at the rooster's call or close to it, before or after, and that is enough. On יום הכפורים, because the כהן גדול may become weak, we do it from midnight. On the רגלים, because there are many people and many sacrifices, we do it from the first watch. This matches the reason taught in the משנה: the rooster's call would not arrive before the courtyard was full of Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי יוחנן's rule to explain why the משנה gives three different start times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah sets no exact hour, the time is chosen by practical need. On a regular day, around dawn is enough. On יום הכפורים, starting at חצות gives the weakened כהן גדול more time, and on רגלים, starting even earlier handles the crowds and the many קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: They remove the ashes from the altar (תרומת הדשן)
The first watch of the night

steps.whatToRemember: There is no Torah-fixed hour for תרומת הדשן, only 'before dawn.' The three times in the משנה (rooster's call, חצות, first watch) are practical choices based on how much work the day requires.

phrases.english: Therefore, every day
they remove the ashes from the altar at the rooster's call
or close to it,
whether before it or after it, that is enough.
On Yom Kippur,
when there is the weakness of the High Priest,
phrases.notes: He does the whole day's service himself, and he is fasting.

phrases.english: we do it from midnight.
And on the Festivals, when the Jewish people are many
and the sacrifices are many,
we do it from the first watch.
As the reason is taught (in the Mishnah):
the rooster's call would not arrive
before the courtyard was full of Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ, בְּכׇל יוֹם תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's flexible rule to explain each time given in the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The start time of תרומת הדשן changes by need. On regular days it is around the rooster's call, on יום הכפורים from חצות, and on רגלים from the first watch.

steps.title: What does קריאת הגבר mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase קריאת הגבר in the משנה means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: the meaning of a word in the משנה. This line sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גבר can mean 'a man' or 'a rooster.' So it is unclear whose 'call' the משנה uses to mark the time.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'call of the gever' (the term being defined)

phrases.english: What is 'kriat hagever'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: defining a term from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'גבר' in the משנה is a man or a rooster.

steps.title: רב says a man's call, רבי שילא says a rooster's call
steps.stepSummary: רב says it is the call of a man. רבי שילא says it is the call of a rooster.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the man's call. רבי שילא said: the rooster's call.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to what קריאת הגבר means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, it is the call of a man: the appointed כהן announced that it was time for the כהנים to come to work. According to רבי שילא, it is the rooster's crow, since a rooster can also be called a גבר. Either way, it marks a time near dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: A man (here, the כהן who called out)

phrases.english: Rav said: the man called.
phrases.notes: The appointed כהן announced the time for service.

phrases.english: Rabbi Sheila said: the rooster called.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: a man calling out (the כהן). רבי שילא: a rooster crowing.

steps.title: רב serves as רבי שילא's speaker and explains 'the call of a man'
steps.stepSummary: רב arrives at רבי שילא's town, steps in as his public speaker, and explains קריאת הגבר as the call of a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב came to the town of רבי שילא. There was no speaker to stand by רבי שילא and repeat his lecture to the people. So רב stood up for him and explained: What is קריאת הגבר? It is the call of a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells a story that shows רב actually teaching his reading from Step 5 in public. This story sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those days a great teacher spoke quietly, and an אמורא (speaker) repeated and explained his words loudly to the crowd. Nobody in town knew רב yet, so he humbly took this helper role. While doing it, he explained קריאת הגבר his own way: the call of a man.

keyTerms.meaning: The speaker who repeats and explains the teacher's lecture out loud to the crowd

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word אמורא does not mean a sage from the גמרא period. It means the speaker who repeats the lecture to the audience (also called a מתורגמן).

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to the place of Rabbi Sheila.

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה אָמוֹרָא לְמֵיקַם עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שֵׁילָא,
phrases.english: There was no speaker to stand over Rabbi Sheila,
phrases.notes: The speaker stood next to the teacher and announced his words to the public.

phrases.english: Rav stood over him and explained:
What is 'keriat hagever'? The call of a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story behind the argument recorded in Step 5, showing רב teaching his reading in public.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב publicly explains קריאת הגבר as the call of a man.

steps.title: רבי שילא corrects רב: say 'rooster'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שילא, not knowing who his speaker is, tells him to say 'the call of a rooster' instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שילא said to him: Let the master say 'the call of a rooster.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שילא challenges the speaker's explanation and offers his own reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שילא holds that the word גבר in the משנה means a rooster, as in Step 5. He corrects his speaker publicly because he thinks the speaker made a mistake. He does not yet know the speaker is the great רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master say (a polite way to suggest a correction)

phrases.english: Rabbi Sheila said to him:
Let the master say: 'The call of a rooster'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רב's explanation in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation of קריאת הגבר as the call of a man
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שילא holds that גבר here means a rooster, so the speaker's explanation is wrong.

steps.title: רב defends himself with a parable and with רבי חייא's silence
steps.stepSummary: רב answers with a folk saying about a flute and adds that רבי חייא heard this explanation and did not object.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: A flute is music to noblemen, but weavers do not enjoy it. When I stood as speaker for רבי חייא and explained 'קריאת הגבר is the call of a man,' he said nothing to me. And you tell me to say 'the call of a rooster'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends his explanation. He says greater scholars accepted it, even if רבי שילא does not appreciate it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flute parable means that fine music is appreciated only by people with refined taste. רב's proof is that his own teacher רבי חייא heard this explanation and stayed silent, which means he agreed. So the reading is good even if רבי שילא rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not say anything to me (he did not object)

phrases.english: He said to him: 'A flute for noblemen is music,
but weavers do not accept it.'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: When I was standing over Rabbi Chiya
and I explained: What is 'keriat hagever'? The call of a man,
he did not say anything to me.
And you tell me: Say 'the call of a rooster'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שילא's correction in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the authority of a greater teacher (רבי חייא) who accepted the reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The speaker's explanation is a mistake, and the word must mean rooster.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reading 'call of a man' was accepted by רבי חייא, so it stands.

steps.title: רבי שילא realizes it is רב and asks him to stop
steps.stepSummary: רבי שילא realizes the speaker is רב and tells him to rest, since serving as his speaker is beneath him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שילא said to him: Is the master רב? Let the master rest.
steps.whatsHappening: Once רב mentions standing before רבי חייא, רבי שילא figures out who he is. Out of respect, he asks רב to stop serving as his speaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רב, the famous student of רבי חייא, could say such a thing. רבי שילא feels it is not fitting for so great a scholar to be his helper. The argument about the word now turns into a story of mutual respect.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is the master Rav?
Let the master rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב's mention of רבי חייא in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the speaker is really רב, together with a request that he step down from the helper role.

steps.title: רב refuses to step down
steps.stepSummary: רב answers with a folk saying (finish the job you took on). Another version says he quoted the rule 'we go up in holiness, not down.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: People say, 'If you hired yourself out to someone, comb his wool.' Some say this is what he told him: 'We raise up in holy matters, and we do not bring down.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains why he will keep serving as the speaker. The גמרא brings two versions of his reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Version one: once you take on a job, you finish it, even the less pleasant parts. Version two: a great scholar has already filled this holy role, so replacing him with a lesser person would lower its honor. That would be disrespectful to the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: If you hired yourself out to him, comb his wool
We raise up in holiness and do not bring down

steps.whyThisMatters: מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין is a well-known halachic principle found throughout ש״ס. Here it is applied to the honor of Torah teaching.

phrases.english: He said to him: People say:
'You hired yourself out to him? Comb his wool.'
Some say this is what he said to him:
'We raise up in holiness, and do not bring down.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שילא's request in Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב will continue as speaker, either because he committed to the job or because one may not lower the level of a holy role.
steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with mutual respect. רב keeps his reading, 'the call of a man,' and stays on as רבי שילא's speaker.

steps.title: There is a ברייתא supporting each side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports רב and another supports רבי שילא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב. A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי שילא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the actual argument and sets up the next move. It will bring outside sources for each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one wins outright. Each reading of קריאת הגבר has a ברייתא behind it. This line is a heading for the sources that follow.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav,
it was taught in accordance with Rabbi Sheila.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the disagreement from Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both readings of קריאת הגבר have support from a ברייתא.

steps.title: The crier גביני supports רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the Temple crier גביני, who called the כהנים, לוים and ישראלים to their duties in a very loud voice. This supports reading גבר as a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רב: What did גביני the crier say? 'Rise, כהנים, to your service; לוים, to your platform; and ישראלים, to your post.' His voice could be heard three פרסאות away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that supports רב. It shows that in the בית המקדש a man's call started the morning work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was a known human crier whose call opened the day, then 'קריאת הגבר' in the משנה most likely means his call, the call of a man. The loud voice shows that this call really could serve as a signal for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: גביני the crier, the official announcer in the בית המקדש
The platform where the לוים sang
The group of ישראלים who stood by the daily offerings
A Persian mile, a unit of distance (about 4 km)

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav:
What did Gevini the crier say?
'Rise, priests, to your service,
and Levites to your platform, and Israelites to your post.'
And his voice was heard at a distance of three parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב: גְּבִינִי כָּרוֹז מַהוּ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the heading in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב's reading that קריאת הגבר means the call of a man
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about גביני the crier's morning call in the בית המקדש

steps.title: אגריפס המלך hears גביני from far away
steps.stepSummary: A story: אגריפס המלך heard גביני's voice from three פרסאות away and sent him gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with אגריפס המלך. He was traveling on the road and heard גביני's voice from three פרסאות away. When he came home, he sent him gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a story that proves how far גביני's voice carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side note backing up the claim about the three פרסאות. The king himself was so impressed that he rewarded the crier.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident / a story that happened
King Agrippa, a king of the Second Temple period

phrases.english: An incident with King Agrippa
who was coming along the road,
and heard his voice at three parasangs,
and when he came home he sent him gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the detail in Step 12 that גביני's voice carried three פרסאות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גביני's voice was heard three פרסאות away, as proven by אגריפס המלך.

steps.title: The כהן גדול's voice carried even farther
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the כהן גדול's voice was greater: his 'אנא השם' was heard in יריחו, which is ten פרסאות from ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the כהן גדול was greater than him. As the master said: He once said 'אנא השם,' and his voice was heard in יריחו. And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: From ירושלים to יריחו is ten פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a comparison: as loud as גביני was, the כהן גדול's voice on יום כיפור reached much farther.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. A source says the כהן גדול's 'אנא השם' in his וידוי was heard in יריחו. Then רבי יוחנן's measurement tells us that is ten פרסאות away, more than three times גביני's distance.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Please, ה׳', the opening words of the כהן גדול's confession on יום כיפור
Jericho, a city east of ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רב: a human crier, גביני, called out each morning in the בית המקדש, which fits reading קריאת הגבר as 'the call of a man.' The comparisons show how strong these voices were.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן, כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְשׁוּבָּח מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: And even so, the High Priest was superior to him.
As the master said:
He once said 'Please, ה׳'
and his voice was heard in Jericho.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
From Jerusalem to Jericho is ten parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן, כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְשׁוּבָּח מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares גביני's voice from Steps 12-13 with the even stronger voice of the כהן גדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול's voice reached ten פרסאות, farther than גביני's three.

steps.title: The כהן גדול was weak and spoke by day
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול's voice carried farther than גביני's even though he was weak from fasting and spoke in the daytime, while גביני was not weak and called out at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is even though here, with the כהן גדול, there was weakness, and there, with גביני, there was no weakness. And here it was daytime, and there it was nighttime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more reasons why the כהן גדול's voice was so impressive compared to גביני's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 compared only distance: ten פרסאות against three. Now the גמרא adds that the כהן גדול was weak from fasting and working on יום כיפור, while גביני was not. It also says the כהן גדול spoke by day while גביני called at night, which sets up the next step's explanation of why that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: weakness (the כהן גדול was weak from fasting and doing the service)

steps.confusionAlert: The text says וְהָכָא ('and here') twice in the first line. The second וְהָכָא actually refers to גביני, meaning 'there.' That is why the translation says 'there.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָכָא אִיכָּא חוּלְשָׁא,
phrases.english: And even though here (the High Priest) there is weakness,
and here (Gevini) there is no weakness.
And here (the High Priest) it was daytime,
and there (Gevini) it was nighttime.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָכָא אִיכָּא חוּלְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens step 14's comparison by adding weakness and time of day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול's voice was greater despite his weakness and despite speaking in the daytime.

steps.title: Why voices carry less during the day
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי teaches that voices are harder to hear by day because the sun makes noise as it moves across the sky, like a carpenter sawing cedars.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי לוי said: Why is a person's voice not heard during the day the way it is heard at night? Because of the sphere of the sun, which saws through the sky like a carpenter sawing cedars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove the claim from the last step that daytime makes a voice harder to hear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 assumed daytime is a disadvantage for being heard. רבי לוי gives the reason: the sun's movement creates a background noise that drowns out voices. So speaking by day really did make the כהן גדול's achievement greater.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין קוֹלוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
phrases.english: Why is a person's voice not
heard during the day
the way it is heard at night?
Because of the sphere of the sun
that saws through the sky
like a carpenter sawing cedars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and supports the 'daytime' point from step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a voice is harder to hear by day than at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי לוי about the noise of the sun.

steps.title: The dust in sunbeams is called 'לא'
steps.stepSummary: The dust seen floating in sunlight by day is called 'לא,' and this explains נבוכדנצר's words that all people of the earth are considered like 'לא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this sawdust of the day, its name is 'לא.' And this is what נבוכדנצר said: 'And all the inhabitants of the earth are considered like לא,' meaning like specks of dust.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the picture of the sun as a carpenter, the גמרא makes a side comment that the specks seen in sunbeams are the sun's 'sawdust.' It then uses this to explain a verse in דניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as sawing makes sawdust, the 'sawing' sun leaves floating specks, which are called 'לא.' This explains the word in דניאל ד:לב: people are as small as dust specks before הקב״ה. It is a side point and does not change the main sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: sawdust, specks of dust (seen in sunbeams)
the name of those dust specks

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'לא' does not mean 'no.' It is the name for dust specks, so the verse means people are like dust, not that they are 'nothing' in the grammatical sense.

phrases.english: And this sawdust (seen) by day,
its name is 'la.'
And this is what Nebuchadnezzar said:
'And all the inhabitants of the earth are considered like la' (Daniel 4:32).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side point growing out of רבי לוי's image of the sun sawing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The floating specks in sunlight are called 'לא,' which explains the verse in דניאל.

steps.title: The sun and the noise of Rome cancel each other out
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the sun's noise drowns out the noise of Rome's crowds, and the noise of Rome drowns out the sun's noise.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Were it not for the sound of the sun's sphere, the sound of the crowds of רומי would be heard. And were it not for the sound of the crowds of רומי, the sound of the sun's sphere would be heard.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is now sounds, the גמרא brings a related ברייתא about two huge sounds that block each other out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building on רבי לוי's idea that the sun makes noise, this ברייתא says another great noise exists: the bustle of Rome. Each one covers the other, so we hear neither.

keyTerms.meaning: the bustle of the crowds of Rome

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Were it not for the sphere of the sun,
the sound of the crowds of Rome would be heard.
And were it not for the sound of the crowds of Rome,
the sound of the sun's sphere would be heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the side discussion of the sun's noise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun's noise and Rome's noise each block out the other.

steps.title: Three sounds that travel across the whole world
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three sounds that travel from one end of the world to the other: the sun, the crowds of Rome, and a soul leaving the body. Some add a woman giving birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Three sounds travel from one end of the world to the other. They are: the sound of the sun's sphere, the sound of the crowds of רומי, and the sound of a נשמה when it leaves the body. And some say: even a birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about sounds. This one lists the sounds that travel across the entire world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of these sounds were already mentioned: the sun and Rome. This ברייתא adds the cry of a נשמה leaving the body. The יש אומרים adds the sound of a woman giving birth, and the list continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: from one end of the world to the other

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Three sounds travel
from the end of the world to its other end,
and these are: the sound of the sphere of the sun,
and the sound of the crowds of Rome,

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹל נְשָׁמָה בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁיּוֹצְאָה מִן הַגּוּף,
phrases.english: and the sound of the soul at the moment it leaves the body,
and some say: even (the sound of) giving birth,
phrases.notes: The list continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁלֹשׁ קוֹלוֹת הוֹלְכִין מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא on the same theme of great sounds, expanding the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three sounds travel across the world: the sun, the crowds of Rome, and a soul leaving the body. Some add birth.
